newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Unisource aims to settle without suing Telefonica.
newsitem.headline: Unisource aims to settle without suing Telefonica.

text.p: The partners in Unisource, the telecoms joint venture grouping carriers from four European countries, aim to settle out of court with Telefonica after it said it would leave the group, a spokesman said on Friday.
"There is a breach of contract. We can settle with them out of court, but if necessary will take other steps," said Ben Verwaayen, head of telecoms at Koninklijke PTT Nederland (KPN).
He was speaking on behalf of the shareholders in Unisource, the pan-European business communications group, which brings together KPN, Telia of Sweden, Swiss Telecom PTT and Telefonica of Spain.
Telefonica said earlier it had formed an alliance with Concert, the partership between British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp.
"They're in clear violation of the nature and the agreements within Unisource," Verwaayen said in a telephone interview.

He dismissed speculation that the withdrawal of Telefonica would jeopardise Unisource's 60/40 venture with AT&T Corp called AT&T Unisource. Verwaayen is chairman of the supervisory board at AT&T Unisource, which competes head on with Concert. "Happily I have in front of me some signed letters from John Walter, the CEO of AT&T saying that the commitment to Unisource and the way forward is unshocked by these events," he said.
"It remains fully in place and has reason to remain in place because we're doing quite well in the market," Verwaayen said.

"Unisource owns the national data network in Spain. Telefonica is a distributor of services of Unisource. Now they have signed with BT that they will be the distributor of Concert, that's contradictory," he said.
Earlier he told CNBC Europe television Telefonica would have to pay up if it abandoned its international alliance.

"We have to work out a lot of these issues together with them. Our aim is to do it in a businesslike fashion, and we'll see what the outcome is," he told Reuters in Amsterdam. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
